349.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: Abū Dharr used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The roof of my house was opened while I was in Mecca. Then Jibrīl descended, opened my chest, washed it with Zamzam water, then brought a golden basin filled with wisdom and faith, poured it into my chest, and then closed it. Then he took me by the hand and ascended with me to the lowest heaven. When I came to the lowest heaven, Jibrīl said to the keeper of the heaven: Open! He said: Who is this? He said: This is Jibrīl. He said: Is anyone with you? He said: Yes, Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is with me. He said: Was he sent for? He said: Yes. When he opened, we went up above the lowest heaven, and there was a man sitting, with dark figures on his right and dark figures on his left. When he looked to his right he laughed, and when he looked to his left he wept. He said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous son! I said to Jibrīl: Who is this? He said: This is Ādam, and these figures on his right and left are the souls of his children. The people of the right among them are the people of Paradise, and the figures on his left are the people of the Fire. When he looks to his right he laughs, and when he looks to his left he weeps. – Then he ascended with me to the second heaven and said to its keeper: Open! Its keeper said to him the same as the first had said, and he opened. Anas said: He mentioned that he found in the heavens Ādam, Idrīs, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Ibrāhīm, may Allah’s blessings be upon them; it is not established how their stations were, except that he mentioned he found Ādam in the lowest heaven and Ibrāhīm in the sixth heaven. Anas said: When Jibrīl passed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by Idrīs, he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous brother! I said: Who is this? He said: This is Idrīs. Then I passed by Mūsā, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous brother! I said: Who is this? He said: This is Mūsā. Then I passed by ʿĪsā, and he said: Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet! I said: Who is this? He said: This is ʿĪsā. Then I passed by Ibrāhīm, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous son! I said: Who is this? He said: This is Ibrāhīm, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Shihāb said: Ibn Ḥazm informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥabba al-Anṣārī used to say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then I was taken up until I rose to a plain where I heard the scratching of the pens.” Ibn Ḥazm and Anas ibn Mālik said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then Allah made fifty prayers obligatory upon my community. I returned with that until I passed by Mūsā. He said: What has Allah made obligatory for your community? I said: He made fifty prayers obligatory. He said: Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that. So He turned to me again and removed half of it. I returned to Mūsā and said: He removed half of it. He said: Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear it. I returned, and He removed half of it. I returned to him, and he said: Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that. I returned to Him, and He said: They are five, and they are fifty; the word is not changed with Me. I returned to Mūsā, and he said: Return to your Lord. I said: I am ashamed before my Lord. Then he took me on until he brought me to the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā); colors covered it, I do not know what they are. Then I was entered into Paradise, and in it were ḥabāyil of pearls, and its soil was musk.”
349.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith stands at the beginning of the Book of Prayer, before the first chapter. Abū Dharr relates what the Prophet told of his journey through the heavens: the opening and washing of his chest, the ascent through the heavens with Jibrīl, and the meetings with Ādam, Idrīs, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Ibrāhīm. Ibn Shihāb adds, through Ibn Ḥazm, statements from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥabba and, together with Anas, the imposition of fifty prayers that were reduced to five. The word ḥabāyil is left untranslated here.

350.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from ʿUrwa ibn az-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, she said: “Allah made the prayer obligatory when He made it obligatory as two rakʿas each, at home and on journey. The travel prayer was kept, and the prayer at home was increased.”
350.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith also stands in the Book of Prayer, before the first chapter. ʿĀʾisha reports that the prayer was first made obligatory as two rakʿas each, at home and on journey; the travel prayer remained as it was, while the prayer at home was increased.

351.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Muḥammad, from Umm ʿAṭiyya, she said: “We were commanded to bring out the menstruating women and the women in their private quarters on the two festival days, so that they might attend the gathering of the Muslims and their supplication; the menstruating women were to keep apart from their place of prayer. A woman said: Messenger of Allah, one of us has no outer garment? He said: Let her companion clothe her with some of her outer garment.” And ʿAbdallāh ibn Rajāʾ said: ʿImrān narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn narrated to us: Umm ʿAṭiyya narrated to us: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say this.
351.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The obligation of wearing clothes in prayer.” Umm ʿAṭiyya reports that it was commanded that on the two festival days the menstruating women and the women in their private quarters be brought out to the gathering of the Muslims; the menstruating women were to keep apart from the place of prayer. A woman without an outer garment is to be clothed by her companion from hers. A further chain follows, introduced with “he said”, through ʿAbdallāh ibn Rajāʾ.

352.matn: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus narrated to us, he said: ʿĀṣim ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Wāqid ibn Muḥammad narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said: Jābir prayed in a waist-wrap that he had tied at the back of his neck, while his clothes were placed on the clothes-stand. Someone said to him: Do you pray in a single waist-wrap? He said: I only did that so that a fool like you would see me. Which of us had two garments in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?
352.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Tying the waist-wrap at the nape in prayer.” Jābir prays in a waist-wrap tied at the back of his neck although his clothes lie on the stand. To the objection he replies that he does it so that a fool like the questioner would see him, and he points out that not everyone had two garments in the time of the Prophet.

353.matn: Muṭarrif Abū Muṣʿab narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī l-Mawālī narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said: “I saw Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh praying in a single garment, and he said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying in a garment.”
353.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Tying the waist-wrap at the nape in prayer.” Ibn al-Munkadir saw Jābir praying in a single garment; Jābir said he had seen the Prophet pray in the same way.

354.matn: ʿUbaydallāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a single garment, having crossed its two ends.”
354.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in a single garment wrapped around oneself.” ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama reports that the Prophet prayed in a single garment whose ends he had crossed.

355.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama: “He saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying in a single garment in the house of Umm Salama, having thrown its two ends over his shoulders.”
355.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Praying in a single garment wrapped around oneself.” ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama reports that he saw the Prophet pray in a single garment in the house of Umm Salama, with its ends thrown over his shoulders.

356.matn: ʿUbayd ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father: ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama informed him, he said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying in a single garment wrapped around himself, in the house of Umm Salama, having placed its two ends on his shoulders.”
356.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Praying in a single garment wrapped around oneself.” ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama reports that he saw the Prophet praying in a single garment wrapped around himself in the house of Umm Salama, with its ends on his shoulders.

357.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us, he said: Mālik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Abū n-Naḍr, the freedman of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydallāh: Abū Murra, the freedman of Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib, informed him that he heard Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib say: “I went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the Conquest and found him washing, while his daughter Fāṭima was screening him. She said: I greeted him, and he said: Who is this? I said: I am Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib. He said: Welcome, Umm Hāniʾ! When he had finished his washing, he stood and prayed eight rakʿas, wrapped in a single garment. When he turned away, I said: Messenger of Allah, my mother’s son claims that he will kill a man whom I have granted protection, so-and-so son of Hubayra. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: We grant protection to whom you have granted protection, Umm Hāniʾ. Umm Hāniʾ said: And that was in the forenoon.”
357.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Praying in a single garment wrapped around oneself.” Umm Hāniʾ reports that she came to the Prophet in the year of the Conquest while he was washing; afterwards he prayed eight rakʿas wrapped in a single garment. She named to him the man whom she had granted protection, and he confirmed that protection. She adds that it was in the forenoon.

358.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra: “A questioner asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about praying in a single garment. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Does each of you have two garments?”
358.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Praying in a single garment wrapped around oneself.” Abū Hurayra reports that a questioner asked the Prophet about praying in a single garment, and the Prophet answered with the counter-question whether each of them had two garments.

359.matn: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from Mālik, from Abū z-Zinād, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, he said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “None of you should pray in a single garment when nothing is on his shoulders.”
359.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If one prays in a single garment, let him put it over his shoulders.” Abū Hurayra transmits from the Prophet the saying that one should not pray in a single garment when nothing is on one’s shoulders.

360.matn: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿIkrima, he said: I heard him, or I had asked him, he said: I heard Abū Hurayra say: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever prays in a single garment, let him cross its two ends.”
360.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “If one prays in a single garment, let him put it over his shoulders.” Abū Hurayra bears witness that he heard the Prophet say that whoever prays in a single garment should cross its ends. In the chain the narrator is unsure whether he heard ʿIkrima himself or asked him about it.

361.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥārith, he said: “We asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh about praying in a single garment. He said: I went out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on one of his journeys, and I came one night on some business of mine and found him praying, while I had on a single garment. I wrapped myself in it and prayed at his side. When he turned away, he said: What is this night travelling, Jābir? I told him of my need. When I had finished, he said: What is this wrapping that I saw? I said: It was a garment – meaning, it was tight. He said: If it is wide, wrap yourself in it, and if it is tight, tie it as a waist-wrap.”
361.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If the garment is tight.” Jābir tells of a night encounter on a journey, when he prayed in his single garment beside the praying Prophet. Asked about the wrapping, he explains that the garment was tight, and the Prophet distinguishes between a wide garment, in which one wraps oneself, and a tight one, which one ties as a waist-wrap.

362.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: Abū Ḥāzim narrated to me, from Sahl, he said: “Men used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with their waist-wraps tied at their necks, like boys, and the women were told: Do not raise your heads until the men are sitting upright.”
362.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “If the garment is tight.” Sahl reports that men prayed with the Prophet with their waist-wraps tied at their necks like boys, and that the women were told not to raise their heads until the men were sitting upright.

363.matn: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, from al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba, he said: “I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and he said: Mughīra, take the water-skin! I took it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went off until he was hidden from me, and relieved himself. He was wearing a Syrian cloak (jubba). He tried to take his hand out of its sleeve, but it was tight, so he took his hand out from underneath. I poured water over him, and he performed his ablution as for prayer, wiped over his khuffs, and then prayed.”
363.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in a Syrian cloak (jubba).” Al-Mughīra tells of a journey on which he carried the water-skin for the Prophet. The Prophet wore a Syrian cloak with tight sleeves, took his hand out from underneath, performed the ablution, wiped over the khuffs, and prayed.

364.matn: Maṭar ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, he said: Rawḥ narrated to us, he said: Zakariyyāʾ ibn Isḥāq narrated to us: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, he said: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh narrate: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was carrying stones for the Kaʿba with them, and he had his waist-wrap on. His uncle al-ʿAbbās said to him: Son of my brother, if only you would undo your waist-wrap and put it on your shoulders, away from the stones! He said: So he undid it and put it on his shoulders, and he fell down unconscious. After that he was never seen naked, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
364.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The dislike of nakedness in prayer and elsewhere.” Jābir reports that the Prophet was carrying stones for the Kaʿba with the others, that his uncle al-ʿAbbās advised him to put the waist-wrap on his shoulders, and that he then fell down unconscious; since then he was never seen naked.

365.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, from Abū Hurayra, he said: “A man stood up before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about praying in a single garment. He said: Does each of you find two garments? Then a man asked ʿUmar, and he said: When Allah grants abundance, act with abundance. Let a man gather his clothes upon himself: a man prayed in a waist-wrap and an upper wrap (ridāʾ), in a waist-wrap and a shirt, in a waist-wrap and a coat (qabāʾ), in trousers and an upper wrap, in trousers and a shirt, in trousers and a coat, in short trousers and a coat, in short trousers and a shirt.” He said: And I think he said: in short trousers and an upper wrap.
365.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in a shirt, trousers, short trousers and a coat (qabāʾ).” Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet answered the question about praying in a single garment with a counter-question. Then an answer of ʿUmar to a similar question is quoted, listing various combinations of garments. The narrator gives the last combination only with “I think.”

366.matn: ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from az-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: “A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: What does the one in iḥrām wear? He said: He does not wear the shirt, nor trousers (sirwāl), nor the burnus, nor a garment that saffron has touched, nor wars. If he does not find sandals, let him wear the khuffs and cut them so that they are below the ankles.” And from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: the same.
366.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in a shirt, trousers, short trousers and a coat (qabāʾ).” Ibn ʿUmar reports that, asked what the one in iḥrām wears, the Prophet excluded the shirt, trousers, burnus and garments touched by saffron or wars, and permitted khuffs, cut below the ankles, for one who finds no sandals. A second chain through Nāfiʿ is joined with “the same.” Wars is a yellow dye.

367.matn: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade the ṣammāʾ wrapping (ishtimāl aṣ-ṣammāʾ) and that a man sit hugging his knees (iḥtibāʾ) in a single garment with none of it over his private part.”
367.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What of the private parts must be covered.” Abū Saʿīd reports that the Prophet forbade the ṣammāʾ wrapping and sitting hugging the knees in a single garment when none of it is over the private part. The two terms are given here in transliteration, untranslated.

368.matn: Qabīṣa ibn ʿUqba narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū z-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two kinds of sales: touching (limās) and throwing (nibādh), and wrapping oneself in the ṣammāʾ manner, and a man sitting hugging his knees in a single garment.”
368.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “What of the private parts must be covered.” Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet forbade two kinds of sales, touching (limās) and throwing (nibādh), as well as the ṣammāʾ wrapping and sitting hugging the knees in a single garment.

369.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: The son of the brother of Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from his uncle, he said: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed me that Abū Hurayra said: “Abū Bakr sent me on that pilgrimage among announcers on the Day of Sacrifice to proclaim at Minā: Beware, after this year no idolater may perform the pilgrimage, and no one may circumambulate the House naked. Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said: Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had ʿAlī ride behind him and commanded him to proclaim Barāʾa. Abū Hurayra said: So ʿAlī proclaimed with us among the people of Minā on the Day of Sacrifice: After this year no idolater may perform the pilgrimage, and no one may circumambulate the House naked.”
369.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “What of the private parts must be covered.” Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Bakr sent him with announcers to Minā on that pilgrimage to proclaim that after this year no idolater may perform the pilgrimage and no one may circumambulate the House naked. Then the Prophet sent ʿAlī after them to proclaim Barāʾa, and ʿAlī proclaimed the same among the people of Minā.

370.matn: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī l-Mawālī narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said: “I entered upon Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh while he was praying in a garment wrapped around himself, with his upper wrap (ridāʾ) laid aside. When he turned away, we said: Abū ʿAbdallāh, you pray with your upper wrap laid aside? He said: Yes, I wanted the ignorant ones like you to see me. I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray like this.”
370.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying without an upper wrap.” Ibn al-Munkadir reports that he saw Jābir praying wrapped in a garment while his upper wrap lay aside. Asked about it, Jābir answers that he wanted the ignorant to see him so, and that he had seen the Prophet pray in the same way.

371.matn: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb narrated to us, from Anas: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went on campaign to Khaybar. We prayed the morning prayer near it in the darkness. Then the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode, and Abū Ṭalḥa rode, and I was riding behind Abū Ṭalḥa. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made his mount run through the lane of Khaybar, and my knee touched the thigh of the Prophet of Allah. Then he drew the waist-wrap back from his thigh, so that I looked at the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah. When he entered the village, he said: Allahu akbar, Khaybar is ruined! When we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned! He said it three times. He said: And the people went out to their work and said: Muḥammad! ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: And some of our companions said: And the army – meaning the army. He said: We took it by force, and the captives were gathered. Then Diḥya came and said: Prophet of Allah, give me a slave girl from the captives. He said: Go and take a slave girl. He took Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy. Then a man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: Prophet of Allah, you gave Diḥya Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy, the lady of Qurayẓa and an-Naḍīr; she is fit only for you. He said: Call him with her. So he came with her, and when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, looked at her, he said: Take another slave girl from the captives. He said: Then the Prophet freed her and married her. Thābit said to him: Abū Ḥamza, what did he give her as dowry? He said: Herself – he freed her and married her. When they were on the road, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and brought her to him at night, and in the morning the Prophet was a bridegroom. He said: Whoever has anything, let him bring it. He spread out a leather mat, and one man came with dates, another came with ghee. He said: And I think he also mentioned barley meal (sawīq). He said: They mixed it into ḥays, and that was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
371.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What is mentioned about the thigh.” Anas reports on the campaign to Khaybar: while riding through the lane the Prophet drew the waist-wrap back from his thigh, so that Anas saw its whiteness. Then follow the taking of Khaybar, the assignment and freeing of Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy, her marriage to the Prophet, and the wedding meal of dates, ghee and barley meal. An addition about “the army” is marked as a remark of some companions of the narrator.

372.matn: Abū l-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from az-Zuhrī, he said: ʿUrwa informed me that ʿĀʾisha said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the dawn prayer, and believing women would attend it with him, wrapped in their cloaks (murūṭ); then they would return to their homes and no one recognized them.”
372.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “In how many garments a woman prays.” ʿĀʾisha reports that believing women prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet wrapped in their cloaks and then returned to their homes without anyone recognizing them.

373.matn: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, he said: Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a garment with markings (khamīṣa), and he glanced once at its markings. When he turned away, he said: Take this garment of mine to Abū Jahm and bring me the anbijānī garment of Abū Jahm; for it distracted me just now from my prayer.” And Hishām ibn ʿUrwa said, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: I was looking at its marking while I was in prayer, and I feared it would tempt me.
373.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If one prays in a garment with markings and looks at its markings.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet prayed in a garment with markings and glanced at them; afterwards he had it sent to Abū Jahm and Abū Jahm’s anbijānī garment brought, because it had distracted him from the prayer. A second chain through Hishām ibn ʿUrwa is joined with “he said.”

374.matn: Abū Maʿmar ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb narrated to us, from Anas: “ʿĀʾisha had a curtain (qirām) with which she had screened one side of her house. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Remove this curtain of yours from us, for its pictures keep appearing before me in my prayer.”
374.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Is prayer invalidated in a garment with crosses or images, and what is forbidden of that.” Anas reports that ʿĀʾisha had screened one side of her house with a curtain, and the Prophet asked her to remove it because its pictures kept appearing before him in prayer.

375.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd, from Abū l-Khayr, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, he said: “A silk farrūj was given as a gift to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; he put it on and prayed in it, then turned away and took it off violently, like one who dislikes it, and said: This is not fitting for the God-fearing.”
375.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who prayed in a silk coat slit at the back and then took it off.” ʿUqba reports that a silk coat slit at the back (farrūj) was given to the Prophet as a gift; he prayed in it, then took it off violently like one who dislikes it, and said that this is not fitting for the God-fearing.

376.matn: Muḥammad ibn ʿArʿara narrated to us, he said: ʿUmar ibn Abī Zāʾida narrated to me, from ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfa, from his father, he said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a red leather tent, and I saw Bilāl take the ablution water of the Messenger of Allah, and I saw the people hurrying to that water; whoever obtained some of it rubbed himself with it, and whoever obtained none took from the moisture of his companion’s hand. Then I saw Bilāl take a spear and fix it in the ground, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out in a red garment, with it tucked up, and prayed two rakʿas with the people facing the spear; and I saw people and animals passing in front of the spear.”
376.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in a red garment.” Abū Juḥayfa reports that he saw the Prophet in a red leather tent, saw Bilāl take his ablution water and the people hurry to it. Then the Prophet prayed two rakʿas with the people in a red garment towards a spear fixed in the ground, while people and animals passed in front of the spear.

377.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥāzim narrated to us, he said: “They asked Sahl ibn Saʿd: What is the pulpit made of? He said: None is left among the people who knows more than I do: it is of tamarisk wood from al-Ghāba; so-and-so, the freedman of so-and-so, made it for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And the Messenger of Allah stood on it when it was made and set up, faced the qibla, said the takbīr, and the people stood behind him; he recited and bowed, and the people bowed behind him; then he raised his head, then went back backwards and prostrated on the ground; then he returned to the pulpit, bowed, raised his head, then went back backwards until he prostrated on the ground. That was his practice.” Abū ʿAbdallāh said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, asked me about this hadith and said: I only wanted that the Prophet was higher than the people; so according to this hadith there is no harm in the imam being higher than the people. He said: I said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna was often asked about this, did you not hear it from him? He said: No.
377.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying on roofs, the pulpit and wood.” Abū Ḥāzim reports that Sahl ibn Saʿd, asked what the pulpit was made of, answered that it was of tamarisk wood from al-Ghāba, and described how the Prophet prayed on the pulpit, bowed, went back backwards and prostrated on the ground. Then follows a report from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh about a conversation with Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, marked as a scholar’s statement and not as a saying of the Prophet.

378.matn: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥīm narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, he said: Ḥumayd aṭ-Ṭawīl informed us, from Anas ibn Mālik: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from his horse, and his leg or his shoulder was scraped, and he swore to keep away from his wives for a month. He sat in an upper room of his, whose steps were of palm trunks. His companions came to visit him, and he prayed with them sitting while they stood. When he gave the greeting of peace, he said: The imam is appointed only to be followed: when he says the takbīr, say the takbīr; when he bows, bow; when he prostrates, prostrate; and if he prays standing, pray standing. He came down on the twenty-ninth, and they said: Messenger of Allah, you swore for a month? He said: The month is twenty-nine.”
378.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter “Praying on roofs, the pulpit and wood.” Anas reports that the Prophet fell from his horse and scraped his leg or shoulder; he prayed sitting before his standing companions and explained that the imam is appointed to be followed. On the twenty-ninth day he came down from the upper room and said the month has twenty-nine days. Whether it was the leg or the shoulder is left open in the report.

379.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, from Khālid, he said: Sulaymān ash-Shaybānī narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Shaddād, from Maymūna, she said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while I was opposite him and I was menstruating, and sometimes his garment touched me when he prostrated. She said: And he used to pray on the khumra.”
379.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If the garment of one praying touches his wife when he prostrates.” Maymūna reports that the Prophet prayed while she was opposite him and menstruating, and that his garment sometimes touched her when he prostrated; he prayed on the khumra, a small prayer mat.

380.matn: ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Anas ibn Mālik: “His grandmother Mulayka invited the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to a meal she had prepared for him; he ate from it, then said: Stand up, that I may pray for you. Anas said: I stood up to a mat of ours that had turned black from long use, and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah stood, and I and the orphan lined up behind him, with the old woman behind us; and the Messenger of Allah prayed two rakʿas for us, then turned away.”
380.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying on a mat.” Anas reports that his grandmother Mulayka invited the Prophet to a meal. After eating, the Prophet called them to prayer; Anas sprinkled a blackened mat with water, the Prophet stood on it, Anas and the orphan lined up behind him and the old woman behind them, and he prayed two rakʿas.

381.matn: Abū l-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān ash-Shaybānī narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Shaddād, from Maymūna, she said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on the khumra.”
381.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying on a small prayer mat (khumra).” Maymūna reports in a short wording that the Prophet prayed on the khumra.

382.matn: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Abū n-Naḍr, the freedman of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydallāh, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, that she said: “I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with my legs in his qibla; when he prostrated he nudged me and I drew in my legs, and when he stood up I stretched them out. She said: And the houses at that time had no lamps.”
382.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying on a bed.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she slept in front of the Prophet with her legs in his qibla; when he prostrated he nudged her and she drew in her legs, and when he stood she stretched them out again. She adds that the houses then had no lamps.

383.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿUrwa informed me: ʿĀʾisha informed him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “used to pray while she was between him and the qibla, on the bed of his family, lying across like a bier.”
383.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying on a bed.” ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet prayed on the bed of his family while she lay across between him and the qibla, as a bier lies across.

384.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd, from ʿIrāk, from ʿUrwa: that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “used to pray while ʿĀʾisha lay across between him and the qibla, on the bed on which the two of them slept.”
384.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying on a bed.” ʿUrwa reports that the Prophet prayed while ʿĀʾisha lay across between him and the qibla on the bed on which both slept. In the chain, the Prophet follows ʿUrwa directly; no transmitter in between is named.

385.matn: Abū l-Walīd Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, he said: Ghālib al-Qaṭṭān narrated to me, from Bakr ibn ʿAbdallāh, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: “We used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of us would place the edge of his garment at the place of prostration because of the intensity of the heat.”
385.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prostrating on one's garment in intense heat.” Anas reports that they prayed with the Prophet and that one of them would place the edge of his garment at the place of prostration because of the intense heat.

386.matn: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Abū Maslama Saʿīd ibn Yazīd al-Azdī informed us, he said: “I asked Anas ibn Mālik: Did the Prophet pray in his sandals? He said: Yes.”
386.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in sandals.” Saʿīd ibn Yazīd asks Anas whether the Prophet prayed in his sandals, and Anas answers yes.

387.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, he said: I heard Ibrāhīm narrate from Hammām ibn al-Ḥārith, he said: “I saw Jarīr ibn ʿAbdallāh urinate, then perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks, then stand and pray. He was asked about it and said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do the same.” Ibrāhīm said: This pleased them, because Jarīr was among the last of those who accepted Islam.
387.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in leather socks.” Hammām reports that Jarīr performed ablution after urinating, wiped over his leather socks and prayed; when asked, he said he had seen the Prophet do the same. The closing remark about Jarīr having accepted Islam late comes from Ibrāhīm, a transmitter in the chain, and is not a saying of the Prophet.

388.matn: Isḥāq ibn Naṣr narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, from al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba, he said: “I helped the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with his ablution; he wiped over his leather socks and prayed.”
388.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in leather socks.” Al-Mughīra reports that he helped the Prophet with his ablution; the Prophet wiped over his leather socks and prayed.

389.matn: aṣ-Ṣalt ibn Muḥammad informed us: Mahdī informed us, from Wāṣil, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ḥudhayfa: “He saw a man who did not complete his bowing or his prostration. When he finished his prayer, Ḥudhayfa said to him: You have not prayed. He said — and I think he said: — If you were to die, you would die on other than the sunna of Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
389.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When one does not complete the prostration.” Ḥudhayfa sees a man who does not complete his bowing and prostration and tells him after the prayer that he has not prayed. The phrase “and I think he said” shows the transmitter’s uncertainty about the wording of the following sentence.

390.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr informed us: Bakr ibn Muḍar narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Ibn Hurmuz, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥayna: that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “when he prayed, held his arms apart until the whiteness of his armpits became visible.” And al-Layth said: Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿa narrated to me the like of it.
390.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Showing the upper arms and keeping them away from the body in prostration.” Ibn Buḥayna reports that the Prophet held his arms apart in prayer until the whiteness of his armpits showed. The addition “And al-Layth said …” is a muʿallaq, that is, given without a complete chain.

391.matn: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us, he said: Ibn al-Mahdī narrated to us, he said: Manṣūr ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Maymūn ibn Siyāh, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever prays our prayer, faces our qibla and eats our slaughtered meat, that is the Muslim who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger; so do not break Allah’s protection.”
391.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of facing the qibla.” Anas transmits a saying of the Prophet: whoever performs the prayer of the Muslims, faces their qibla and eats their slaughtered meat is under the protection of Allah and His Messenger, and this protection must not be violated.

392.matn: Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Ḥumayd aṭ-Ṭawīl, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah. When they say it, pray our prayer, face our qibla and slaughter as we slaughter, then their blood and their property are forbidden to us except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah.”
392.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of facing the qibla.” Anas transmits a saying of the Prophet: he was commanded to fight the people until they pronounce the testimony of faith; whoever says it, performs the prayer of the Muslims, faces their qibla and slaughters as they do, his blood and property are inviolable except by right, and his reckoning is with Allah.

393.matn: Ibn Abī Maryam said: Yaḥyā informed us: Ḥumayd narrated to us: Anas narrated to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
393.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places this chain under the chapter “The virtue of facing the qibla.” It is introduced with the formula “Ibn Abī Maryam said” and contains only the chain up to the Prophet, without a wording of its own.

393.2.matn: And ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh said: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, he said: Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: “Maymūn ibn Siyāh asked Anas ibn Mālik and said: O Abū Ḥamza, what makes the blood of a servant and his property inviolable? He said: Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, faces our qibla, prays our prayer and eats our slaughtered meat, he is the Muslim; he has what the Muslim has, and upon him is what is upon the Muslim.”
393.2.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī gives this report under the chapter “The virtue of facing the qibla” in the form “And ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh said.” Maymūn asks Anas what makes blood and property inviolable; Anas answers that whoever pronounces the testimony of faith, faces the qibla, performs the prayer and eats the slaughtered meat is a Muslim with the same rights and duties.

394.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: az-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī: that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you go to relieve yourselves, do not face the qibla and do not turn your backs to it, but face east or west. Abū Ayyūb said: We came to Syria and found latrines built facing the qibla; so we would turn aside and ask forgiveness of Allah, the Exalted.” And from az-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ, he said: I heard Abū Ayyūb from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.
394.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The qibla of the people of Medina and of Syria.” Abū Ayyūb transmits the Prophet’s saying that when relieving oneself one should neither face the qibla nor turn one’s back to it, but face east or west. The following account about the latrines in Syria is a statement of the Companion Abū Ayyūb about his own conduct. At the end follows a second chain from az-Zuhrī via ʿAṭāʾ with a similar wording.

395.matn: al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, he said: “We asked Ibn ʿUmar about a man who had circumambulated the House for ʿumra but had not walked between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwa: May he go to his wife? He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived, circumambulated the House seven times, prayed two rakʿas behind the Station, and walked between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwa; and you have in the Messenger of Allah a good example.”
395.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The saying of Allah: ‘And take the station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.’” Ibn ʿUmar answers a question about ʿumra, pointing out that the Prophet circumambulated the House seven times, prayed two rakʿas behind the Station of Ibrāhīm and walked between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwa; he concludes by referring to the example of the Messenger of Allah.

396.matn: And we asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh, and he said: “Let him not approach her until he has walked between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwa.”
396.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places this statement under the same chapter. It stands without a chain of its own as a continuation of the previous report: to the same question Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh answers that one should not approach one’s wife until one has walked between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwa.

397.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sayf, he said: I heard Mujāhid say: “Ibn ʿUmar was approached and told: Here is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who has entered the Kaʿba.” Ibn ʿUmar said: So I came, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had already come out, and I found Bilāl standing between the two doors. I asked Bilāl and said: Did the Prophet pray in the Kaʿba? He said: Yes, two rakʿas between the two pillars that were on his left as you enter; then he came out and prayed two rakʿas facing the front of the Kaʿba.
397.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The saying of Allah: ‘And take the station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.’” Mujāhid reports that Ibn ʿUmar was told the Prophet had entered the Kaʿba. Ibn ʿUmar asks Bilāl, who confirms that the Prophet prayed two rakʿas between the two pillars on the left of one entering, and then two more rakʿas in front of the Kaʿba.

398.matn: Isḥāq ibn Naṣr narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd ar-Razzāq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners and did not pray until he came out of it. When he came out, he prayed two rakʿas facing the Kaʿba and said: This is the qibla.”
398.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Ibn ʿAbbās reports that on entering the House the Prophet made supplication in all its corners and prayed two rakʿas in front of the Kaʿba only after coming out; he said that this is the qibla.

399.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Rajāʾ narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, loved to be turned toward the Kaʿba. So Allah revealed: ‘We see you turning your face about in the heaven,’ and he turned toward the Kaʿba. And the fools among the people, that is, the Jews, said: ‘What has turned them away from their qibla, which they had been following?’ Say: ‘To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path.’ Then a man prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and went out after he had prayed, and passed by some people of the Anṣār who were praying the ʿaṣr prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis. He said, bearing witness, that he had prayed with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he had turned toward the Kaʿba. So the people turned until they faced the Kaʿba.”
399.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Facing the qibla wherever one is.” Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, then the Qurʾānic verse about the turning of his face in the heaven was revealed and he turned toward the Kaʿba. A man who had prayed with the Prophet told some of the Anṣār during the ʿaṣr prayer, and they turned toward the Kaʿba. The uncertainty “sixteen or seventeen” comes from the transmission.

400.matn: Muslim narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from Jābir, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on his mount in whatever direction it turned; but when he wanted to pray the obligatory prayer, he would dismount and face the qibla.”
400.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Facing the qibla wherever one is.” Jābir reports that the Prophet prayed on his mount in whichever direction it faced; for the obligatory prayer he dismounted and faced the qibla.

401.matn: ʿUthmān narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, he said: ʿAbdallāh said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed — Ibrāhīm said: I do not know whether he added or omitted — and when he had given the salām, it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, has something new occurred in the prayer? He said: What is that? They said: You prayed such and such. So he folded his legs, faced the qibla, prostrated twice and then gave the salām. When he turned to us with his face, he said: Had something new occurred in the prayer, I would have informed you of it; but I am only a human being like you, I forget as you forget. So if I forget, remind me; and if any of you is in doubt about his prayer, let him seek what is correct, complete on that basis, then give the salām, then prostrate twice.”
401.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Facing the qibla wherever one is.” ʿAbdallāh reports that the Prophet prayed; when he was asked whether something new had occurred in the prayer and was told that he had prayed such and such, he faced the qibla, prostrated twice and gave the salām. Afterwards he said that he was a human being like them and forgets, that they should remind him, and that whoever is in doubt in prayer should seek what is correct. The transmitter Ibrāhīm’s uncertainty whether the Prophet prayed more or less is preserved in the wording.

402.matn: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, he said: ʿUmar said: “I agreed with my Lord in three things: I said: O Messenger of Allah, if only we took the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer! So there was revealed: ‘And take the station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.’ And the verse of the ḥijāb: I said: O Messenger of Allah, if only you would command your wives to veil themselves, for both the righteous and the wicked speak to them! So the verse of the ḥijāb was revealed. And the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, united in jealousy over him, so I said to them: ‘Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you.’ So this verse was revealed.” Ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us, he said: Ḥumayd narrated to me, he said: I heard Anas say this.
402.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What has come about the qibla.” Anas transmits a statement of ʿUmar that he agreed with his Lord in three things: the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer, the verse of the ḥijāb, and the verse about the wives of the Prophet, which was revealed after his words. A second chain through Ibn Abī Maryam follows, in which Ḥumayd says he heard it from Anas.

403.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik ibn Anas informed us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, he said: “While the people were at Qubāʾ in the morning prayer, someone came to them and said: Qurʾān was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Kaʿba, so face it. Their faces were toward Syria, so they turned around toward the Kaʿba.”
403.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What has come about the qibla.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that the people of Qubāʾ learned during the morning prayer that the Prophet had been commanded to face the Kaʿba; they, who had been facing Syria, turned around toward the Kaʿba.

404.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbdallāh, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed the Ẓuhr prayer with five rakʿas. They said: Has the prayer been increased? He said: What is that? They said: You prayed five. So he folded his legs and prostrated twice.”
404.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What has come about the qibla.” ʿAbdallāh reports that the Prophet prayed the Ẓuhr prayer with five rakʿas; when he was asked whether the prayer had been increased and was told that he had prayed five, he folded his legs and prostrated twice.
